title: Bud Light Boycotters Are Still Waiting for Their ‘Woke-Free’ Beer
gist: Wired reports that Ultra Right Beer, launched in 2023 as a 'woke-free' Bud Light alternative, left about 400 Facebook-group customers waiting for limited-edition orders, drew an F rating from the BBB, and is under Georgia attorney general investigation.

insights.claim: Seth Weathers launched Ultra Right Beer in April 2023 before securing a brewery, claimed near $1 million in six-pack sales at $19.99, and later partnered with Big Kettle Brewing.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Outrage-driven demand can be monetized before any operating capability exists.

insights.claim: Ultra Right Beer LLC has an F rating from the BBB for failing to answer nearly 200 complaints, and Georgia's attorney general has opened an investigation citing unresponsiveness to compliance orders.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: State-level enforcement is the main downside for political-affinity direct-to-consumer brands.

insights.claim: Customers say Fight-edition orders from 2024 never arrived, with about 400 people in a Facebook group still waiting and resellers listing empty six-packs for up to $115.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Collectible demand for political merchandise outlives fulfillment, creating secondary-market speculation.
insights.quote: People Still Waiting for Ultra Right Fight Beer

insights.claim: Buyers interviewed say they bought for collectibility rather than the Bud Light boycott, and blame the founder as a scammer who traded on partisan identity.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Affinity marketing is an effective fraud and trust vector, which may chill future partisan consumer brands.

insights.claim: Anheuser-Busch filed a trademark opposition in 2024 citing similarity to Michelob Ultra, still ongoing, which Weathers blamed for delays.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Large incumbents can use IP litigation against challenger brands while they struggle operationally.

insights.claim: Contract brewer Ironshield Brewing, operator of Big Kettle Brewing, announced it was shutting down in December 2023, removing the production partner.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Asset-light brands depend on fragile contract manufacturers.
